investigate: Scientific argumentation is hard to improve in traditional classes because of ==individual differences==.
The authors built an ==AI agent based on the CER+R framework== to support personalised, data-driven practice.
Eighteen Ecology students in eastern China used the agent either before or after practising independently in a ==crossover design==.
find: Students who ==practised independently before using the agent== showed more interactive and constructive engagement.
Among the 12 students with complete test data, argumentation performance ==improved significantly== from pre-test to mid-test and post-test.
Rebuttals often lacked later evidence or reasoning, so the authors suggest ==additional scaffolding== is needed.

caption.question: Can an AI agent help students argue like scientists?
caption.intro: Liu, Zong, Zhao and Wang compare **an AI agent built on the CER+R framework** with independent practice in a crossover study of 18 university Ecology students in eastern China.
